name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just upstream noise—it’s that auto-applying whitespace patches to third-party code introduces silent divergence from upstream, making future updates harder to merge. A safer alternative is to enforce formatting standards in your own codebase via CI checks, not runtime patches. Settle it by proving the cost of manual formatting fixes in your repo outweighs the risk of dependency drift.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk is that Pret’s parser may misinterpret whitespace in ways that subtly corrupt third-party code—like mistaking a tab for spaces in a critical section. A better alternative is to fork the dependency, apply formatting once, and pin the fork in your lockfile—no runtime patching, no parser dependency. Settle it by testing Pret on a sample of your largest third-party dependencies and measuring merge conflicts before and after.
